summary: Hemet sits on the floor of the San Jacinto Valley, a broad inland basin east of the San Jacinto Mountains, where the horizon stretches wide in every direction and evening light pours down western ridgelines with almost theatrical clarity — nearly 10 hours of daily sunshine on average keeps the sky dominant year-round, with daytime highs averaging 77°F and mild lows around 54°F that make the climate feel like a drier, calmer version of the Inland Empire's heat. What makes the numbers here genuinely unusual is the home-price-to-income ratio: a median home value of $314,200 against a median household income of $53,623 yields roughly a 5.9× ratio, which is strikingly accessible by Southern California standards, though that income also means a median rent of $1,432 still claims about 32% of gross pay. The local economy leans heavily on healthcare — Hemet Valley Medical Center is a major employer — along with retail and public-sector jobs, but a bachelor's-degree attainment rate of just 15.2% signals a labor market with limited white-collar depth, so many workers commute west toward Temecula, Riverside, or beyond. The city sprawls across 29 square miles at a modest density, connected more by wide arterial roads than walkable grids, though Diamond Valley Lake to the south and the San Jacinto Wildlife Area offer genuine outdoor access without a long drive. Hemet is a place where Southern California sunshine and relative affordability coexist with the commute costs and infrastructure tradeoffs that affordability usually implies.
